description:
We are Team TerraBeats from Cajamarca, Peru, tackling "The Earth Information Jukebox" challenge. We are a multidisciplinary group of developers, sound enthusiasts, and science communicators combining frontend engineering (React 19), real-time Web Audio DSP (Tone.js), computer vision, and universal accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AAA).

Our project transforms silent NASA satellite visualizations into interactive, real-time musical soundscapes and narrated documentaries.
summary:
NASA's Earth Information Center (EIC) showcases our changing planet through breathtaking satellite imagery, yet over 2.2 billion people worldwide living with visual impairments cannot access this visual data. TerraBeats is an accessible, bilingual (English/Spanish), and fully offline-capable web jukebox that transforms five EIC satellite visualizations into interactive real-time soundscapes and narrated documentaries—turning silent Earth science into music.

Running entirely in the browser without pre-rendered audio files, TerraBeats analyzes video frames at 30 fps using client-side computer vision (HTML5 Canvas). It translates physical Earth measurements—GEDI forest canopy height, sea surface temperature, lightning activity, urban night lights, and atmospheric carbon dioxide—into dynamic musical synthesizers via Tone.js and the Web Audio API.

TerraBeats integrates three complementary layers: intuitive auditory icons, musical data mapping, and synchronized educational narration generated with open-source neural voice synthesis (Kokoro, Apache 2.0). Listeners can explore the globe with full keyboard navigation, compare two moments in time to hear what changed, feel lightning bursts through mobile haptic vibration, and customize visual accessibility with a dedicated Low-Vision panel. TerraBeats enables anyone—blind or sighted—to hear our planet breathe.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

TerraBeats is an open-source, client-side web application that transforms silent NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations into interactive, real-time soundscapes and educational audio documentaries. Running 100% inside the browser, it processes video frames every 33 ms (~30 fps) across an end-to-end mathematical pipeline:

  1. Client-Side Frame Ingestion & CORS Resolution: Video streams of NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) releases are hosted locally as web-optimized MP4 files to bypass browser cross-origin canvas security restrictions (getImageData).
  2. Canvas Downsampling & UI Masking: Each frame is drawn to an offscreen 160×90 HTML5 Canvas (OffscreenCanvas / 2D context). This downscaling reduces computational overhead to 14,400 RGBA evaluations per tick, ensuring a smooth 60 Hz interface across laptops and smartphones. Dynamic bounding boxes mask out on-screen text overlays, timestamps, and static legends.
  3. Computer Vision & Calibrated Feature Extraction: An extraction engine (src/analysis/features.js) scans every pixel and classifies it against official NASA scientific color ramps, computing global coverage, calibrated physical units, 16-column spatial density profiles, and inter-frame temporal deltas.
  4. Algorithmic Sound Synthesis (Tone.js / Web Audio API): Extracted values modulate polyphonic synthesizers (Karplus-Strong plucks, dual-operator FM chimes, detuned sawtooth clusters, and membrane percussion). All notes are strictly clamped to pentatonic and modal scales to eliminate chaotic dissonance.
  5. Temporal Comparison & Regional Exploration: Users can bookmark two points in time (Key M) to hear what changed between them (src/analysis/compare.js), jump directly to regional hotspots such as the Humboldt current or Amazon basin (Key X), or explore the globe freely with spatial ray-casting audio labels.
Project Flow & Architecture (Based on the System Diagram)
Detailed Pipeline Description:
  1. NASA Data Input: Ingests authentic scientific visual data from five flagship EIC missions: GEDI LiDAR canopy height, ECCO2 sea surface temperature and currents, ISS Lightning Imaging Sensor (LIS), Suomi NPP VIIRS Black Marble night lights, and GEOS DYAMOND atmospheric CO2.
  2. Frame Processing: Resolves browser CORS restrictions by hosting optimized MP4 videos locally. A 30 fps render loop draws each active frame onto an offscreen 160×90 HTML5 Canvas (14,400 pixels/tick) while masking out static graphic timestamps, color bars, and visual borders.
  3. Computer Vision & Feature Extraction: Executes mathematical color classification via illumination-invariant Look-Up Tables (GEDI 0–50 m), HSV Hue trigonometric conversion (SST 0–32 °C), and 16-column spatial density profiling.
  4. Real-Time Audio Generation: Modulates polyphonic synthesizers (Karplus-Strong plucks, FM bells, saw clusters, membrane kicks) via Tone.js and the Web Audio API, quantized to musical scales with dynamic voice ducking (−9 dB) and master brickwall limiting (−2 dBFS).
  5. Educational Audio: Synchronizes bilingual (English/Spanish) educational documentary narration synthesized locally using the open-weights Kokoro-82M neural TTS model (Apache 2.0).
  6. Accessible Jukebox & Multimodal Output: Delivers a fully inclusive experience through ARIA 1.2 screen-reader regions, a "See Better" Low-Vision panel, "Compare Two Moments" (Key M), regional exploration (Key X), and mobile haptic vibration feedback.
  7. Technology Foundation: Built entirely upon modern open standards: JavaScript (ES2023+), React 19, HTML5 Canvas, Tone.js, Web Audio API, Kokoro TTS, and a Progressive Web App (PWA) Service Worker for 100% offline functionality.
Methodology & Work Plan

Our project utilized an Iterative Agile Development Framework tailored for a 40-hour hackathon cycle, structured across four specialized sprints:

Sprint 1: Scientific Research & Data Ingestion (Hours 0–8):

  • Downloaded high-resolution NASA SVS visualization master videos.
  • Sampled official color calibration bars to construct exact Look-Up Tables (LUTs) for GEDI and ECCO2.
  • Re-encoded videos via FFmpeg to lightweight web MP4s (0.4–4.6 MB) to solve CORS restrictions.

Sprint 2: Algorithmic Vision & Audio Architecture (Hours 8–20):

  • Implemented the 30 fps Canvas extraction loop (features.js).
  • Constructed the Tone.js modular synthesizer matrix (engine.js), harmonic scales, and ducking buses.
  • Developed spatial ray-casting algorithms on Natural Earth 1:50m marine boundaries (geo.js).

Sprint 3: Accessibility, Storytelling & Local Neural Voice (Hours 20–32):

  • Wrote bilingual (ES/EN) educational scripts fact-checked against NASA SVS mission logs.
  • Generated 148 static narration audio cues locally using the Kokoro-82M model (Apache 2.0).
  • Built the "See Better" Low-Vision panel, "Compare Two Moments" delta engine, and mobile touch D-Pad.

Sprint 4: Validation, Offline PWA & Cloud Deployment (Hours 32–40):

  • Conducted blindfold user comprehension testing (4-question protocol).
  • Implemented Service Worker caching (sw.js) for a 52 MB offline standalone experience.
  • Completed WAI-ARIA 1.2 audits with NVDA, JAWS, and TalkBack, deploying to the Vercel Edge Network.

What benefits does it have?

  1. Dual Accessibility (Blind & Low-Vision):
    • For Non-Sighted Users: 100% keyboard operability, ARIA 1.2 screen-reader regions, single-voice priority rules (no overlapping voices), and tactile mobile crosshairs.
    • For Low-Vision Users: A dedicated "See Better" (Ver mejor) accessibility panel with high-contrast modes, large and extra-large scalable typography, an animations toggle (prefers-reduced-motion), and an audio-only mode.
  2. Dual-Coding Science Comprehension: Combining visual satellite data with intuitive auditory cues reinforces learning, helping sighted students and educators recognize complex thermal and atmospheric dynamics faster than through visual inspection alone.
  3. Temporal Change Perception ("Compare Two Moments"): Users can mark moment A and moment B with Key M; the system computes the exact scientific difference between the two frames and speaks/sonifies the delta, revealing the planet's change over time.
  4. 100% Offline Capability (PWA): A built-in offline package (52 MB, 186 files cached via Service Worker sw.js) ensures that TerraBeats functions seamlessly as an installable application without an active internet connection.
  5. Zero Infrastructure Cost & Client-Side Privacy: No external cloud processing or GPU servers are required. No user data, keystrokes, or audio queries leave the visitor's device.
  6. Replicable Open-Science Standard: Researchers, planetariums, and museums can sonify any NASA SVS dataset simply by providing an MP4 video, a calibrated color LUT, and a JSON narrative cue sheet.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Measurable Educational Comprehension Benchmark:

We developed a standardized acoustic testing framework to verify that non-sighted users can acquire genuine scientific knowledge solely through listening. After a 2-minute sonified story, a participant is evaluated on four core questions:

  • Q1 (Forests): Where are the tallest forests concentrated? (Target: Amazon, Congo Basin, Southeast Asia)
  • Q2 (Oceans): Does the warmest water stay near the Equator or move toward the poles? (Target: Concentrated near the Equator, oscillating with seasons)
  • Q3 (Lights): Which major country showed the greatest luminous expansion from 2012 to 2023? (Target: India)
  • Q4 (CO₂): What cycle does carbon dioxide follow throughout the day? (Target: It pulses—absorbed by day, released by night)

Benchmark Target: ≥75 accuracy (at least 3 of 4 correct answers) without visual assistance.

Societal & Institutional Reach:

  • Interactive Science Kiosks: Drop-in accessible software for exhibits at the Smithsonian, planetariums, and NASA Earth Information Center installations.
  • Inclusive STEM Classrooms: Empowers teachers to integrate blind students directly into climate and Earth observation curricula.
  • Regional Scalability from Cajamarca, Peru: Demonstrates that high-impact, universally accessible space technology can be engineered in regional Latin America and deployed globally.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

How is your project creative?

  • Real-Time Generative Synthesis vs. Static Soundtracks: Conventional projects place pre-recorded background music over science videos. TerraBeats computes audio from scratch every 33 ms directly from visual pixels. If a city lights up or a storm clears, the sound changes immediately.
    1. Auditory Icons: Natural acoustic phenomena recognized instinctively (thunder, waves, forest birds, electrical hum).
    2. Data-Driven Musical Layer: Strict scalar mappings (pitch = canopy height or sea temperature, volume = density, stereo pan = longitude) constrained to pentatonic scales to prevent dissonant noise.
    3. Synchronized Narrative Ducking: Spoken documentary voiceover that automatically ducks background music by −9 dB.
  • Auditory Legend & Sonified Ruler: Before playback begins, users can audition each instrument in isolation and hear the artistic rationale behind its acoustic design ("A lightning flash is instantaneous, which is why it is rendered as percussive staccato").
  • Temporal Delta Comparison (Key M): Allows users to compare two moments in time, listening to acoustic and spoken summaries of how global conditions evolved between them.
  • Regional Discovery Mode ("My Region", Key X): Provides instant navigation to regional observation zones (such as the Humboldt current off Peru or the Amazon rainforest), grounding global data in local relevance.
  • Space Observatory Aesthetic: A sleek mission control interface featuring CSS-animated starfields and planetary orbits that automatically adjust for users with prefers-reduced-motion.

What factors did your team consider?

  1. 100% Open Source Compliance (NASA Terms & Conditions): To strictly adhere to NASA Space Apps 2026 rules requiring all non-NASA project assets to be free or open-source (OSI-approved), we eliminated proprietary speech services and adopted Kokoro (Apache 2.0 open-weights neural TTS). All 148 narration clips and 10 episodes were synthesized locally on our own machines without transmitting text or data to commercial third-party cloud APIs.
    • Screen-Reader Harmony: All controls operate via keyboard without mouse hover dependencies; mobile TalkBack/VoiceOver touch drag interception was resolved by providing an on-screen tactile D-Pad.
    • Dedicated Low-Vision Controls: A "See Better" panel allows users to enlarge text, toggle high contrast, and disable animations.
    • Single-Voice Hierarchy: Help audio, welcome speech, documentary narration, and quizzes never overlap; opening help pauses the active story.
  2. Acoustic Aesthetics vs. Auditory Fatigue: Raw sonification often sounds abrasive. We constrained frequencies to pentatonic/modal scales, added spatial stereo depth, and applied a soft-knee glue compressor with a brickwall limiter at −2 dBFS to ensure pleasant listening over consumer headphones.
  3. Digital Inclusion in Regional Peru: Developed in Cajamarca, Peru, where internet access can be slow or intermittent, video sizes were kept between 0.4 and 4.6 MB, and a 52 MB offline caching pack (PWA) was implemented so the application runs completely offline in remote classrooms.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI) Declaration

AI tools were utilized strictly in accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines:

  1. Code and Documentation: We used large language model assistants (Claude by Anthropic) to assist in refactoring React components, optimizing canvas pixel processing routines, and drafting bilingual technical documentation. All algorithmic logic, color calibration pipelines, and audio mappings were conceived, supervised, tested, and validated by our team.
  2. Narrator Voice: The scripted narration voiceover was generated locally using Kokoro (an open model with Apache 2.0 weights, version 82M: voices ef_dora for Spanish and af_heart for English). The speech was synthesized on our own computer using kokoro-onnx and espeak-ng. No text, prompts, or personal data were sent to any commercial speech service. The generated audio files are stored locally as static MP3 clips. Interactive quiz feedback, live remarks, and coordinate labels are synthesized in real time by the visitor's browser via the native Web Speech API.
  3. Zero AI-Generated Images, Videos, or Music: No generative AI tools were used for media creation. All visual assets are authentic scientific visualizations from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS), and 100% of the music and sonification is generated live by our custom Tone.js algorithmic code directly from video pixels.

Project Development Schedule & Milestones

Team Roles & Technical Contributions

eam Roles & Technical Contributions (Cajamarca, Peru)

  • Daniela Miranda (Project Lead & Frontend Software Engineer):
    • Directed overall software architecture and hackathon execution.
    • Built the React 19 component hierarchy, track state machines, and the "See Better" Low-Vision accessibility panel.
    • Configured Vite build optimizations, Service Worker PWA caching, and automated Vercel cloud deployment.
    • Fact-checked all narration against NASA Scientific Visualization Studio documentation and peer-reviewed mission data.
    • Authored bilingual (English/Spanish) educational documentary scripts, audio legends, and real-time interactive quiz questions.
    • Synchronized narration cue timestamps with specific video events across all 5 tracks.
    • Engineered the Web Audio DSP graph and modular Tone.js synthesizer matrix.
    • Calibrated musical scale quantization (pentatonic and modal) to eliminate acoustic dissonance.
    • Programmed the −9 dB dynamic voice ducking bus, master glue compressor, and −2 dBFS brickwall limiter.
    • Developed the HTML5 Canvas 30 fps pixel extraction pipeline and dynamic bounding-box graphic masking.
    • Implemented the illumination-compensated Look-Up Table (LUT) matching algorithm for GEDI forest canopy height.
    • Coded trigonometric HSV Hue angle conversion for sea surface temperature and the "Compare Two Moments" delta engine.
    • Implemented WAI-ARIA 1.2 semantic roles (aria-live="polite", role="status", aria-pressed) and full keyboard navigation.
    • Conducted screen-reader accessibility audits using NVDA, JAWS, and mobile TalkBack/VoiceOver.
    • Developed the on-screen mobile touch D-Pad and integrated the Web Vibration API for haptic lightning feedback.

Representative Code Architecture

1. Frontend & Visual Accessibility: src/components/ViewOptions.jsx

Provides low-vision users with instant toggles for high contrast, scaled typography (large/extra-large), and reduced motion, persisted via localStorage:

2. Client-Side DSP Audio Engine ("Backend" in Web Audio): src/audio/engine.js

Implements the entire Web Audio API graph using Tone.js: polyphonic synthesizers, dynamic voice ducking (−9 dB), a master soft-knee glue compressor, and a brickwall peak limiter (−2 dBFS):

3. Computer Vision & Photometric Calibration: src/analysis/features.js

Extracts pixels from an offscreen HTML5 Canvas at 30 fps and performs illumination-invariant matching against NASA’s official color bar:

4. Temporal Delta Analytics ("Compare Two Moments"): src/analysis/compare.js

Averages a rolling 25-frame window (~2 seconds) between Moment A and Moment B (Key M) to compute true planetary changes:

5. Offline PWA & Byte-Range Slicing: public/sw.js

Enables the application and all cached media (52 MB) to run completely offline by handling HTTP byte-range slicing for smooth seeking:

6. Local Neural Voice Synthesis: scripts/build-narration-kokoro.py

Ensures 100% open-source compliance under NASA Space Apps Challenge terms by generating all voice assets locally using the Kokoro-82M ONNX model (Apache 2.0):

Project Conclusion & Scientific Outlook

TerraBeats proves that cutting-edge NASA Earth observations do not have to remain locked behind silent visual media. By combining client-side computer vision, real-time mathematical sonification, local open-source neural voice synthesis, and universal design principles (WCAG 2.1 AAA), our team has created an interactive bridge between raw satellite science and human perception.

Key Accomplishments:

  • True Universal Access: Over 2.2 billion people living with visual impairments can independently listen to, explore, and comprehend complex planetary dynamics—from the height of the Amazon rainforest to global sea surface temperatures.
  • 100% Open Science & Privacy: Released under the Apache License 2.0, using exclusively open-source models (Kokoro-82M) and self-hosted assets, guaranteeing zero commercial data tracking and complete compliance with NASA Space Apps rules.
  • Resilience in Regional Environments: Designed and built in Cajamarca, Peru, TerraBeats includes a 52 MB offline PWA pack, proving that high-impact scientific accessibility tools can run in low-connectivity rural classrooms anywhere in the world.

TerraBeats transforms passive visual observation into active, inclusive listening. It is not merely a jukebox—it is an accessible auditory observatory that allows all of humanity to hear our planet breathe.
